*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Curated parallels for the sutta's verse are found across multiple Buddhist traditions in the seventeenth chapter (*Udakavarga*, "Water") of the *Udānavarga*, preserved in Sanskrit (UVS 17), Tibetan (*Uv Kg* 17), and Chinese canonical collections (*Chuyao jing*, T 212.18; *Faji yaosong jing*, T 213.17). In addition, automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies substantial shared phraseology across 46 Pali texts; the narrative and prose formulas share extensive segments with the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16, particularly matching segments §4.2–4.5 of Ud 7.9 with DN 16 §4.23.6–4.24.4) and the *Cunda Sutta* (Ud 8.5), along with standard phrasing shared with the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 8, AN 6, AN 5, AN 3) and the *Majjhima Nikāya* (MN 82, MN 91, MN 92) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments also link the text to Śāntideva's *Śikṣāsamuccaya*, the Chinese *Dīrghāgama* (T 1), and the Chinese *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra* (T 7) [DharmaNexus]. Secondary literature matching the search query solely discusses the common noun *udapāna* (a well or well-hall) in Vinaya architectural regulations and epigraphy, without addressing this sutta directly.
